sections.html:
The Broward County Property Appraiser sets assessed values and approves exemptions. It does not mail tax bills and does not set or collect taxes. Billing and collection belong to the Broward County Tax Collector, at (954) 357-4829 or revenue@browardtax.org, as printed on the appraiser's home page.

Deed recording runs through the county's official records. The appraiser's FAQ page has a deed topic for questions on adding or removing an owner or getting copies of recorded documents. Counter service is on weekdays.

Broward has 31 municipalities, and Fort Lauderdale is the seat and biggest city, with 183,146 residents. A canal-front home near Las Olas and a condo in a western city share one appraiser and one tax collector but sit in very different markets, so a neighbor's sale price may say little about yours.

The timely filing period for the 2027 exemption runs March 3, 2026 through March 1, 2027. It applies to owners who held title and made the house their permanent home after January 1, 2026.

An owner who misses March 1 has until September 20, 2027. Section 196.011(8) allows no later date, even with good cause. The dates belong to one tax year, so check the appraiser's page for later years.

The appraiser's site has several tools a home sale can use.

  • A Home Buyer's Tax Estimator that approximates the bill after a reassessment. A seller can use it to show a buyer why their taxes will differ.
  • A Portability Estimator for owners moving a homestead benefit to a new Florida home.
  • Owner Alert, a free message when a filing that changes who owns your parcel reaches the appraiser.
  • A catastrophic structural damage report form for a home left uninhabitable for at least 30 days by a catastrophic event.
  • Tabs for Senior Citizens, Appeals and Petitions, Market Sales and Important Dates, and a posted Property Owner Bill of Rights.

The menu also lists Exemption Express, Download Forms, Tangible Property, Maps and Aerials, Data Requests and a Report Fraud page. A seller who rents out furnished space can start at Tangible Property, and anyone who suspects a forged deed can use the fraud page together with Owner Alert. A buyer notice on the site tells purchasers not to expect the seller's taxes to carry over, since the new owner starts at full market value.

sections.h2: Selling or moving with a homestead
sections.html:
The sale ends the homestead cap on the old house. Someone buying another Florida home can file Form DR-501T alongside the new application, provided the new homestead starts inside the three-year window. A 2026 act amends the portability section for the 2027 roll, so ask the appraiser's portability staff what applies to your move.

Rentals face a yearly ceiling of 10 percent, so a landlord's gap between assessed and market value is usually narrower than a long-time homesteader's.

Age and veteran relief varies by ordinance and service record. The Senior Citizens tab on the appraiser's site is the quickest way to see what a particular address can claim. The state also offers a $5,000 reduction for disabled former servicemembers, and a deferral through the collector with a March 31 filing date.

sections.h2: If a Broward bill goes unpaid
sections.html:
Delinquency starts April 1, and the collector auctions certificates for the lowest bid rate by June 1. If a tax deed notice arrives, call the collector right away. A seller who clears the balance before any deed application avoids the auction altogether, and the title agent can pay it from sale proceeds. Homestead rules on small balances and opening bids sit in s. 197.502.

Before you list, ask the collector for a current payoff figure and confirm nothing is outstanding. A clean tax record keeps the closing simple, and a cash buyer will usually want the same confirmation.

The appraiser's Appeals and Petitions section lays out the route. A formal petition goes to the clerk. Property owners get 25 days from the August notice, and an exemption denial carries its own 30 day clock from the letter.

Gather recent comparable sales and photos of any condition problems before you file, and bring them with your petition.

sections.h2: Paperwork to bring to the office
sections.html:
Whether you visit the appraiser, the collector or the exemption desk, arrive with a photo ID, your parcel number, a copy of your deed and your most recent tax bill. If you are applying on behalf of a seller who has died or moved away, bring whatever proof of your authority you have. A prepared folder shortens the visit and cuts down on return trips.

Closing agents also like to receive tax payoff figures in writing, so request a printed or emailed statement and not just a number over the phone.

An heir can call the appraiser at (954) 357-5579 to learn how a transfer on death is treated, since some transfers are exceptions to the reset.

Uninvited occupants are a separate matter. The sheriff handles a verified complaint under s. 82.036, which carries conditions such as no tenancy and no pending litigation, and adverse possession (s. 95.18) needs seven years. If occupants are holding up a sale, talk to a Florida attorney before you list.

A short checklist saves trouble at closing. Pull your latest tax bill and your exemption paperwork. Confirm with the tax collector that nothing is owed. Decide whether a buyer will be told about the reassessment, and print the estimator result if you plan to share it. Then give your title agent the parcel ID and the name of anyone who may need to sign.

At the closing table, the title agent normally prorates the year's taxes between you and the buyer and pays off any lien from your proceeds. Ask for the settlement statement ahead of time and read each tax line.

sections.h2: Selling for cash with taxes owed
sections.html: A cash sale skips lender underwriting, so a back tax balance doesn't stall a loan approval. It still has to be paid, usually out of proceeds at closing. If you are behind, ask the collector for a payoff figure, give it to the title agent, and confirm the lien is released after funding. Keep the receipt with your closing papers.

sections.h2: How the county's history touches a sale
sections.html: Broward became Florida's 51st county on October 1, 1915, carved out of Dade and Palm Beach territory. Northern Dade residents had complained that their tax dollars favored Miami, which helped push the new county into being.

faqs.a: The Broward County Tax Collector. The appraiser neither sends bills nor collects taxes.

faqs.q: What is the late-filing limit for a 2027 Broward homestead?
faqs.a: September 20, 2027, with no later date allowed under s. 196.011(8).

faqs.q: Can I file my Broward homestead online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the appraiser's online homestead page at bcpa.net. Email, fax, mail and phone help are also available, and staff can set a virtual meeting for owners who want help with the forms.
It's a free service that notifies you when a document changing your property's ownership reaches the appraiser. It is meant to help protect a parcel from scams or fraud.

faqs.q: When does a Broward bill turn delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1, with certificates sold by June 1.
